items.rationale: The theft-damaged frame is covered at the cost of a like-grade replacement under §§7.1.7(b) and 7.1.9. The EUR 3,500 agreed value replaces the EUR 500 class cap under §4.4; it is a ceiling, not a fixed payment.

The brakes were damaged in the theft, so §§7.1.7(b) and 7.1.9 allow a standard-equivalent replacement set, with fitting assessed separately. The scheduled value does not reduce the estimated repair total.
Section 7.1.7(f) covers necessary freight for the replacement parts or the bicycle, but §7.1.8(g) bars recovery transport billed twice. The estimate is for one necessary parts shipment.
Sections 7.1.7(g) and 7.1.8(f) allow a necessary repair attendance distinct from the locksmith's recovery visit. The estimate is for one local visit if its purpose is documented.

Frame and brake fitting, alignment and testing are covered under §7.1.7(c). The estimate allows ordinary frame-transfer and fitting work, excluding any labour already charged separately under §7.1.8(g).

Section 7.1.7(e) covers small fixings and consumables used in the repair, but §§7.1.8(d) and 7.1.10 exclude shop overhead and unsupported charges. The estimate is a modest allowance for repair materials.
Section 7.1.7(d) covers one necessary apprentice hour at the customary rate, provided it is not already included in assembly under §7.1.8(g).
Section 7.1.7(d) covers one necessary skilled repair hour at an ordinary bicycle-workshop rate, excluding time already billed under assembly per §7.1.8(g).

The on-site locksmith attendance was necessary to recover the bicycle and is covered under §5.2.2(a). One visit is estimated at EUR 40, consistent with Case 23; the recovery costs are below the EUR 1,000 cap.

Under §§5.2.2(b) and 7.1.10, the charge is assessed by its purpose: cutting and removing the seized lock to release the bicycle. The estimate follows the comparable recovery operation in Case 23 and excludes duplicated hourly labour.

Section 5.2.2(b) covers materials actually consumed in releasing the lock, not the locksmith's tools or general overhead under §7.1.8(d). If substantiated, the allowance is EUR 7, consistent with Case 23.
Section 5.2.2(b) covers necessary lock-release labour at every grade. One apprentice hour is estimated at EUR 35.50 using Case 23, provided it is not already charged in the flat fee.

Section 5.2.2(b) covers skilled lock-release labour, but §7.1.8(g) excludes time already included in the operation charge. If separately substantiated, EUR 40 for the hour is consistent with the upper bound in Case 23.
